name: Mir Hasan
bio: The book gives his name as Mir Shulam Hasan (that is, Ghulam Hasan), born at Delhi, who passed his youth in Faizabad and then came to Lucknow to join the literary circle there. It describes him as handsome in person as in mind, and says his verse is still popular. He wrote as Hasan.

The one piece given here is drawn from Hindustani Lyrics (London: The Sufi Publishing Society, 1919), in the English verse of Inayat Khan and Jessie Duncan Westbrook. It is a free rendering, not a literal translation, and the original Urdu poem is untitled; it is named here by its first line.

poems.title: Like silver torrents flow thy words to me
poems.author: Mir Hasan
poems.translator: trans. Inayat Khan and Jessie Duncan Westbrook (1919)
poems.text:
Like silver torrents flow thy words to me,
But ah--I have no voice to answer thee.

My heart thy words have burnt with whips of fire,
Do they not burn thy lips, O Heart's Desire?

Thy promises are broken every day,
Yet--See my faithfulness!--I hear you say.

Candle-like wastes my body all these days
My flame-like tongue endures to sing thy praise.

O Hasan, I have spoke and sighed and sung,
Yet never from my heart my tale was wrung,
My secret grief can never find a tongue.
